_meta.phase_gating: T1-T5 completed for the whole passage before T6-T9 began, per the technique doc
_meta.built_from: technique doc T1-T9 applied directly to the source extract row data; not modelled on prior verse-reading output files (Obadiah/Hosea passes)
open_scoping_calls: T6 IB-stamp scope for pro-drop verb subjects (person morphology only, no separate pronoun row) -- this pass stamps action only, not IB, on such rows (v9 perish=we, v10 turned=they). Not settled by the doc's text.

T8 Process scope broadened to physical/ritual state-objects tied to an IB (sackcloth, ashes, throne, robe, hands, way, violence, disaster-as-threatened-fate) but not to spoken/decreed content-objects (message, decree, proclamation, deed). Judgment call, not confirmed.

t1_t5.reading: The word of the LORD came-to-be (Qal wayyiqtol, HVqw3ms, root hayah) to Jonah, a second time, saying [the speech that follows]. 'Word' is grammatical subject of the coming-to-be event; the LORD is the word's source (construct 'word-of-LORD'); Jonah is the goal; 'saying' is the standard formula introducing the direct speech that follows in v2.

flags.readings: T2: stepGloss reads flatly 'to be', but the operative sense is the lexicon's own 'to happen, fall out, occur, come to pass' -- the formulaic prophetic-word-event sense, stated directly in the lexical range, not inferred.

T5: repeats the book's own opening commissioning formula (cf. Jon 1:1), explicitly marked 'the second time' -- genre-conventional signal of a renewed commission after chs.1-2, recorded rather than read as incidental repetition.

t1_t5.reading: Three Qal imperatives, 2ms (HVqv2ms), address Jonah: Arise, go to Nineveh ('that great city'), call out against it. The message clause 'that I tell you' uses H1696G as a Qal participle (HVqrmsa), not a finite verb -- the message's own words are not yet supplied.

flags.readings: T3: participle carries durative in-the-moment force -- 'the message that I am [in the act of] speaking to you' -- not 'will tell'/'have told'; the load-bearing correction of the verse.
T4: no referent crux -- 'you' (2ms) is unambiguously Jonah, matching the imperatives.
T5: commission (v2) defers actual proclamation content to v4 -- delayed disclosure is a structural/genre feature, recorded rather than read as an omission.

t1_t5.reading: Jonah arose and went to Nineveh (Qal wayyiqtol 3ms x2), 'according to the word of the LORD' -- compliance with v2. Disjunctive aside follows: 'Now Nineveh was a city great to/for God [idiom], three days' journey [in extent].'

flags.readings: T1/T2: surface gloss 'exceedingly' is actually 'God' (H0430G, Elohim) + lamed prefix -- the Hebrew superlative idiom 'great to/of God', not a distinct adverb lexeme. H0430G's own lexical range is entirely 'the Deity' entries; the superlative force comes from the construction, not a hidden sense of God. Flagged so the row isn't read as an independent participant.

T3: Qal PERFECT, not wayyiqtol -- breaks the narrative chain carrying 'arose'/'went', producing the English 'Now...' as a background/circumstantial aside, not a further narrated event. Stated from the morph.
T5: city-size aside is a stock scene-setting device; recorded because it sets up the scale problem the narrative exploits in v4 (a one-day proclamation inside a three-day city).

t1_t5.reading: Jonah began (Hiphil wayyiqtol 3ms) to go into the city, one day's journey [in]; he called out and said (two Qal wayyiqtol 3ms verbs as one reporting unit): 'Yet forty days, and Nineveh [is] overthrown.'

flags.readings: T2: stepGloss doubles as 'to profane/begin'; full range dominated by profane/defile senses. 'Begin' is specifically the Hiphil entry (morph HVhw3ms confirms), stated directly for that stem -- not connected to the profane-sense cluster otherwise filling the entry.

T3: Niphal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, feminine singular (agreeing with Nineveh) -- not a finite future verb. Per the technique doc's own caution on participles, reads as durative/imminent ('is on the verge of being overthrown'), a nuance a finite yiqtol would not carry.

T5: the oracle (v4b) is bare and unconditional, five Hebrew words, no stated 'unless you repent' clause -- an absence a reader might expect from the genre; conditionality only surfaces in v9 and is confirmed retroactively by v10. Recorded rather than passed over.

t1_t5.reading: The people of Nineveh (collective, H0582) believed God (Hiphil wayyiqtol 3mp), called for a fast, and put on sackcloth (both Qal wayyiqtol 3mp) -- 'from their greatest to their least.' Corporate, immediate, city-wide response; no individual named yet.

flags.readings: T2: stepGloss reads 'be faithful', but operative sense is the Hiphil-specific 'to stand firm, to trust, to be certain, to believe in' -- distinct from the Qal/Niphal 'support, confirm, be established' senses dominating the rest of the entry. Stated directly for this stem.

T2: bare Elohim form, not H3068 (YHWH) used for the LORD's own speech in vv1,3 -- the text itself marks the shift (different Strong's codes) between the commissioning LORD and the generic 'God' the Ninevites perceive/respond to. Recorded as a lexical fact, not smoothed into one referent.
T5: 'from the greatest to the least' is a stock merism marking totality of response; recorded as doing that structural work.

t1_t5.reading: The word reached the king of Nineveh (introduced here for the first time, H4428G). A tight chain of the king's own acts follows, all Qal/Hiphil wayyiqtol 3ms: arose from his throne, removed his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, sat in ashes.

flags.readings: T2: stepGloss 'to pass: bring'; full range dominated by 'to pass over/through/by'. Causative 'bring/carry/take away' is specifically Hiphil; with 'his robe' as object, operative sense is 'caused [his robe] to pass off him' = 'took off' -- the lexicon's own stated causative sense for this stem.

T3: Qal ACTIVE, not a Niphal/Hithpael reflexive, though the entry lists reflexive senses elsewhere. Reflexive force is carried by the prepositional chain ('upon him') rather than the verb stem -- 'he covered [sackcloth] upon himself'. Matters for comparison with v8's different stem/mood for the population's covering.

T4: the king is never named anywhere in Jonah -- an open naming gap, but not a T4 crux (no competing referent candidates; every 3ms form points unambiguously to 'the king'). Recorded as observation, not resolved as ambiguity.
T5: the four-part sequence (arise/remove robe/cover with sackcloth/sit in ashes) is a stock royal mourning/humiliation ritual formula; recorded as one conventional unit.

t1_t5.reading: He (the king, continued from v6) issued a proclamation and had it published throughout Nineveh: 'By the decree of the king and his nobles/great-ones [lit. "his great-ones", built on the ordinary adjective "great"]: let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not feed or drink water...'

flags.readings: T1: literally H1419A ('great', the same root as 'great city' in vv2-3) + 'and' -- 'his great-ones', not a separate title-word. Flagged so it isn't read as an unrelated court-title lexeme.
T3: jussive mood 3mp, matching the decree's own imperatival force ('let them not...'), not simple future statements -- a mood distinction from the morph, not just the English 'let'.
T5: extending the fast to animals ('man and beast... herd nor flock') goes beyond typical human-only fasting convention; recorded as the text's own marked excess (total civic mourning).

t1_t5.reading: [Decree continues] '...but let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and let them call out mightily to God. Let everyone/each turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in their hands.'

flags.readings: T2: stepGloss 'man', but lexical range explicitly includes 'each (adjective)... whosoever' -- the distributive 'each one' sense used here is lexicon-stated directly, not inferred. The base gloss 'man' alone would mislead toward a specific singular male.

T3: distinct stem/mood from the king's own Qal active 'covered...himself' in v6 (HVqw3ms). Here the decree commands the populace to BE covered/cover-themselves (jussive reflexive-passive) -- grammatically different from the king's individual active act, even though both render 'covered...with sackcloth' in English.

T3: morph-tagged 3rd person MASCULINE PLURAL ('their'), not singular, though the printed ESV reads 'his hands'. Per T3 (morph decides, not the English), the reading is 'the violence that is in THEIR hands', matching the distributive 'everyone/each' two words earlier. Direct correction to the surface translation.

T4: not a referent crux (both suffixes plainly point to the same distributive populace), but an internal grammatical-number variation (3ms then 3mp) within one clause about the same subject -- recorded, not passed over.

T5: pairs a general reorientation ('his evil way') with one specific named sin ('violence') -- both conventional elements of a repentance call; the specificity of 'violence' is the text's own chosen concretization.

t1_t5.reading: 'Who knows? God may turn and relent, and turn from his burning anger, so that we do not perish.' A three-verb chain (turn/relent/turn) describes an uncertain hoped-for divine action, followed by a 1cp purpose clause.

flags.readings: T2: stepGloss itself states this term is 'always used of God's anger' -- lexically restricted to divine anger, not a generic intensity term. Named explicitly rather than treated as ordinary.

T3: 'knows' (H3045, HVqrmsa) is a Qal active participle ('who [is] knowing'), stative/durative, matching the rhetorical-question idiom. The two occurrences of 'turn' (H7725O) carry two different morph tags -- HVqi3ms (first) and HVqq3ms (second) -- though both render 'turn' in English; flagged as a form distinction in the source data, not treated as identical repetition, pending fuller morph-code confirmation. 'Perish' (H0006, HVqi1cp) confirms the 1cp ('we') subject.

T4 referent crux: person is fixed (1cp) but WHO is included is not. Three grammatically live readings: (a) the king and his court; (b) the king voicing the fate of the whole city, given the city-wide decree just issued (vv7-8); (c) a general proverbial 'we'. Reading (b) adopted as primary given the immediate context; (a) and (c) kept on record as grammatically possible but contextually weaker -- not eliminated.
T5: 'Who knows?' is a recognized OT idiom of hope offered without presumption of guaranteed mercy; recorded as doing that conventional work, not rhetorical filler.

t1_t5.reading: God saw their deed(s) -- [lit. a noun phrase, not a finite verb clause in that row] -- namely that they turned (Qal PERFECT 3cp, subordinate/background) from their evil way; God relented (Niphal wayyiqtol 3ms, main narrative line resumes) of the disaster that he had said (Piel perfect 3ms) he would do to them, and he did not do it (Qal perfect 3ms).

flags.readings: T1: surface gloss 'they did' reads as if finite, but the actual Strong's/morph is H4639K (ma'aseh, 'deed, work' -- a noun, HNcmpc, construct) + H0853 (DDO marker): literally '[he saw] the-deeds-of...', a construct noun phrase as object of 'saw', not an independent verb clause. The finite content-verb ('turned') is the NEXT row. Flagged so the row isn't mistaken for a second finite clause.

T2: same base root, two different sub-entries -- H7451I is the ethical/moral sense ('evil, injury, wrong'), H7451C here is the harm/calamity sense. The lexical data preserves a deliberate wordplay: the Ninevites' moral 'evil way' (turned from) and God's threatened 'disaster' (relented of) share one root, tagged by two different sub-senses -- named explicitly rather than flattened into one gloss.

T3: 'turned' is PERFECT, not wayyiqtol -- grammatically subordinate/background within the object of 'saw', not a separate main-line event, matching 'how they turned' as explanatory. 'Said' is PIEL perfect, not Qal -- the lexicon lists '(Piel) to speak; to promise' as distinct from Qal's plainer 'to speak, declare, converse', tying God's earlier oracle (v4) to a formally spoken/declared register, stated from the stem.
T4: unambiguous -- anaphoric chain runs back to 'the people of Nineveh' (v5) via 'they turned' here; no live crux.

T5: resolution-formula of an averted-judgment oracle ('God saw... God relented... he did not do it') -- a recognized structural close. Closes the repentance-oracle unit opened at v4, and retroactively confirms v4's oracle was implicitly conditional even though v4 itself stated no condition (per the T5 flag there) -- conditionality is demonstrated narratively here, not stated propositionally anywhere in the passage.
